newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricketer Shane Warne has criticised West Indian batsman Brian Lara for his behaviour during the fifth test in Perth last week, saying he broke the players' unwritten code by speaking out during a match. Page 18.

Canberra Raider's utility back Jason Crocker could be out of rugby for three months after breaking his arm in last night's Super League trial match between the Raiders and Penrith in Fiji. Penrith beat the under-strength Raiders 26-24. Page 18.

In the lead-up to this week's Australian Master's Golf Tournament, world number one golfer Greg Norman has warned 21 year-old American sensation Tiger Woods not to burn himself out as the demands on his time increase. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD
New South Wales rugby union five-eighth Scott Bowen looks set to miss early matches of this year's Super 12 series after sustaining a shoulder injury in training last week. Page 46.

The Australian cricket team arrived in Johannesburg yesterday for the up-coming test series against South Africa amid a markedly reduced security presence compared with the 1994 tour. The series has been touted an unofficial world championship with Australia and South Africa regarded as the two best teams in the world. Page 46.

Following the success of the Sydney Swans last year, chief executive Wayne Jackson has predicted Sydney could be the home of a second Australian Football League club by the year 2000, possibly playing out of Homebush Stadium. Page 45.
THE AGE

A consultant's report has found Australian Football League clubs could earn up to A$300,000 a game at Docklands stadium, but many clubs still fear a move could upset grass-root supporters and compromise sponsors. Page C8.
Bart Cummings trained horse Saintly will carry 61 kg in the AJC Doncaster to be raced at Randwick on March 29 after carrying only 55.5 kg when it won the Melbourne Cup last year. Page C6.
Australian cyclist Patrick Jonker will represent his country of birth The Netherlands in international competition after cycling for Australia at the last two Olympic Games. Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN

Former Australian cricketer Merv Hughes has been ruled out of playing for Victoria in this Sunday's Mercantile Mutual Cup match against New South Wales despite recent good form in Melbourne grade cricket. Victoria's chairman of selectors John Grant said that despite Hughes' 37 wickets this season, he has "no chance in the world". Page 66.

Tight security has been planned for today's golfing pro-am in the lead-up to this week's Australian Masters after predictions of 10,000 spectators, many of whom are hoping to catch a glimpse of tournament favourite, Tiger Woods. Page 70.
Owners of the horse Doremius have conceded the up-coming Australian Cup to Melbourne Cup winner Saintly, and are instead running the horse in the Ranvet Stakes at Rosehill two days earlier. Page 65.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH
Australian tennis players Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde are the third and sixth highest money earners respectively this year, with Woodbridge earning A$221,200 and Woodforde A$168,432. Page 58.

Former Australian rugby league captain Mal Meninga will be inducted into the Australian Sports Hall of Fame this month. Meninga, who coaches the Canberra Raiders, holds points scoring records at both state and test levels. Page 56.

National Basketball League champions South East Melbourne have signed East Michigan University player Brian Tolbert as theirs second import player to replace American Bill McCaffrey who did not take up the optional second year of his contract. Page 55.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
